query: Why do handling times differ by channel and priority?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue plausibly drives both which channel/priority a ticket lands in (treatment routing) and how long it takes to handle (outcome), so it is a common cause not stated in the query.

per_column.name: operational_urgency
per_column.rationale: Genuine operational urgency influences the assigned priority (treatment) and independently affects handling time via escalation and effort, making it a common cause surfaced from the text. It is distinct from the nominal 'priority' field named in the query.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity plausibly shapes both routing to a channel/priority and the intrinsic time to resolve, a classic common cause not named in the query.

per_column.name: scope_of_impact
per_column.rationale: Breadth of impact affects prioritization (treatment) and the workload/handling time (outcome), so it is a plausible common cause not in the query.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: The technical domain of the fault can drive which channel/team and priority it goes to and the resolution effort, a common cause; some risk of being a mediator of complexity but treated as an upstream categorical cause.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Whether a workaround exists influences urgency-based priority assignment and reduces pressure/time on handling, plausibly a common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The treatments (channel and priority) are the columns already present in the query, and every added column supplies a plausible common cause of both routing/prioritization and handling time. Crucially, none of these confounders (issue type, urgency, complexity, scope, root-cause domain, workaround availability) were named or implied in the query, which only mentioned channel and priority. They are genuine upstream common causes rather than mediators on the treatment->outcome path or colliders, so the set demonstrates real causal-attribution reasoning by surfacing adjustment variables from the ticket text. Minor risk exists that technical_complexity/root_cause_domain partly mediate each other, but each remains a plausible confounder for the channel/priority->handling_time attribution.
